transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-06-15
Time: 16:00 PDT
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Aisha Patel (Redwood AE), Connor Lee (Redwood SE), Maria Gomez (Solaris Head of Infrastructure), Ethan Wu (Solaris Security Architect), Priya Shah (Solaris Platform Engineer), Samir Rao (CTO)

Optional auto sections:
Summary: Solaris is assessing Redwood Private for payment-processing helper endpoints. They need VPC peering or private endpoints, strict egress controls, and KMS-managed keys. They asked about region constraints and DR.
Topics: VPC peering vs PrivateLink, IP ranges, KMS, SOC2, onboarding timeline.
Action items: see metadata above.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Aisha Patel: Hi everyone, thanks for taking the time. Quick roll call 24. If you can just say name and role.
[00:10] Maria Gomez: Maria Gomez, Head of Infrastructure at Solaris.
[00:13] Ethan Wu: Ethan Wu, Security Architect.
[00:15] Priya Shah: Priya Shah, Platform.
[00:17] Samir Rao: Samir Rao, CTO.
[00:18] Aisha Patel: Great, Connor and I are from Redwood, Connor's our SE, I'll be your AE. Today we wanted to focus on private deployment details 24 networking, peering, endpoints, region limits 24 things that matter for PCI-adjacent workloads.
[00:34] Connor Lee: Yeah hi all. High level, Redwood Private runs a customer-controlled control plane in your VPC or a customer VPC peered to Redwood, we support peering, PrivateLink style private endpoints, and in some cases dedicated egress IPs. We'll walk through tradeoffs.
[00:48] Maria Gomez: We're evaluating hosted vs dedicated vs private. For our card-data flow we need full isolation and controllable egress IPs. Can you tell us how peering works and what we keep vs what Redwood operates?
[01:05] Connor Lee: Sure. In the typical model we can either peer Redwood's VPC with your VPCs and run service instances in our side with route tables, or we can deploy a customer-managed bundle that runs inside your VPC in a private subnet (on-prem or VPC). Peering: you manage the ingress/egress rules on your side; we rely on the peering connection and announce routes. PrivateLink: we provide network interfaces in your account and you connect to the ENIs 24 that reduces route-table changes but needs endpoint policies.
[01:35] Ethan Wu: With peering, can you guarantee static egress IPs? Our firewall team needs outbound allowlists for third-party payment rails.
[01:43] Connor Lee: We can't guarantee arbitrary static egress from a peered setup without NAT in your VPC. For static egress we recommend either a customer-managed NAT Gateway in your VPC (so all outbound leaves with known IPs), or Redwood can provide NAT egress through a set of advertised IPs in the region 24 that second option is available under Dedicated Reserved or specific Private offers with assigned egress IP ranges.
[02:06] Maria Gomez: That makes sense. If we go with customer NAT, that keeps control on our side which I prefer. What about KMS integration? Keys must be customer-controlled.
[02:16] Aisha Patel: Redwood Private supports customer KMS/HSM integration. You can bring your own KMS keys. For hosted we manage keys but for Private we can integrate with your AWS KMS (granting necessary role permissions) or use an HSM vendor via network link.
[02:33] Priya Shah: Ok so we'd have to set up IAM roles and key policy to allow Redwood's runtime to decrypt model caches? Can you be specific on the least-privilege permissions?
[02:43] Connor Lee: We'll provide an IAM policy template 24 get, decrypt, describe for the key alias, and we recommend a specific role that we assume via STS. We'll send the template post call.
[02:55] Samir Rao: Region question: we operate in eu-west-1 and us-east-1 primarily; are your private deployments regional? Can we pair for DR across regions?
[03:05] Connor Lee: Yes deployments are regional. We can deploy a primary in eu-west-1 and a secondary in us-east-1. For cross-region failover we support multi-region routing with health checks; it's an add-on pattern but has been done for other customers. There are data residency implications though 24 you'll want to discuss which data stays in region.
[03:25] Ethan Wu: Audit logs 24 we need streaming of audit logs to our SIEM, long retention (7+ years in some cases). What's available?
[03:34] Aisha Patel: Redwood provides audit logs and request/response traces for Private installs and can stream logs to your S3 or a syslog endpoint. Retention is configurable. We'll share the logging architecture doc.
[03:45] Maria Gomez: On networking, we have overlapping CIDRs with some partners. Does peering require non-overlapping ranges?
[03:53] Connor Lee: Yes peering requires non-overlapping CIDR ranges. If you have overlap we recommend PrivateLink endpoints or a customer-side NAT/proxy to translate. We'll talk through a pathing option in the diagram.
[04:08] Priya Shah: What about service limits 24 e.g., how many concurrent connections, throughput per instance? We run bulk ingestion for fraud models and need predictable latency.
[04:18] Connor Lee: For Private we size dedicated pools per your throughput SLOs. We'll run load profiles and recommend instance flavors; we also support quantized model variants to reduce memory. For predictable latency we recommend pinned instances or dedicated GPU pools. We'll propose a perf benchmark plan.
[04:37] Maria Gomez: Perfect. On security, does Redwood support SAML/SSO and SCIM for provisioning?
[04:42] Aisha Patel: Yes SSO via SAML and SCIM provisioning supported for Private installs; RBAC is customizable. We'll provide an SSO integration guide.
[04:51] Ethan Wu: A few clarifying questions 24 traffic egress to payment processors: do you provide IP allowlist ranges for egress from Redwood-managed egress? If yes, are those ranges regional static blocks?
[05:03] Connor Lee: When you choose Redwood-managed egress (a paid add-on), we publish regional IP blocks and can provide a shorter list for allowlisting. Without that add-on, you should NAT through your own infrastructure to control egress addresses.
[05:18] Maria Gomez: For PrivateLink, is there any additional latency compared to peering?
[05:23] Connor Lee: PrivateLink adds minimal hop but in practice latency delta is small 24 ms level 24 but depends on region and cross-AZ routing. We can include latency numbers from previous benchmarks.
[05:33] Priya Shah: We also have strict compliance around logging of PII and redaction. Can Redwood redact at the runtime or do we need to handle before sending?
[05:42] Aisha Patel: Redwood offers configurable pre-request filters and PII redaction pipelines in the Private deployment. For sensitive PII we recommend client-side redaction when possible, but we can also attach redaction rules in the pipeline and log redaction proofs.
[05:58] Samir Rao: Timeline: if we wanted to pilot in a non-prod VPC next quarter, what's the typical onboarding time?
[06:05] Connor Lee: For a pilot (non-prod) with provided subnets and IAM roles, onboarding typically takes 2-4 weeks: infra setup (1 week), config and security review (1 week), perf validation and tuning (1-2 weeks). Enterprise installations with air-gapped setups take longer.
[06:20] Maria Gomez: Any gotchas around AWS endpoints like AWS PrivateLink quotas or ENI limits?
[06:26] Connor Lee: Good point 24 PrivateLink uses ENIs and you need free ENI quotas in your subnets. We'll include recommended subnet sizing in our diagram and checklist.
[06:36] Ethan Wu: Are you able to do VPC peering to a transit gateway instead of direct peering? We use a TGW hub-and-spoke design.
[06:44] Connor Lee: Yes, we support peering to a TGW as long as routing is allowed and the TGW attachments permit cross-account peering. There are additional route propagations to consider. We'll call out TGW in the network doc.
[06:56] Maria Gomez: Ok next 24 data ingress. We stream some logs into the model for lookups; does Redwood require those to transit your control plane? Can we keep data on our side and just call the APIs?
[07:08] Aisha Patel: You can keep data in your VPC and call Redwood endpoints. For reduced egress/ingress we support deploying feature-store connectors inside your VPC so the runtime reads directly from your data stores; that pattern is common for low-latency lookups.
[07:23] Priya Shah: Good. On the networking diagram, we need to see which ports need to be open, what CIDR ranges Redwood will use if we pick managed egress, and which roles to create.
[07:33] Connor Lee: We'll provide a checklist: required ports, sample security group rules, IAM role template, KMS policy template, and sample PrivateLink configuration.
[07:44] Maria Gomez: About region pairing 24 is there support for multi-AZ and multi-region replication for KV cache?
[07:52] Connor Lee: KV cache is local to region for latency reasons; for multi-region you'd replicate or warm caches across regions 24 we can orchestrate replication but it requires cross-region data movement and you'll want to review data residency.
[08:05] Ethan Wu: Any customer references in payments or fintech who've run Private?
[08:09] Aisha Patel: We can share redacted references 24 there are a few fintechs in our references who run dedicated/private installs with strict egress controls. I'll get permission and share.
[08:19] Maria Gomez: Pricing 24 is Private a one-time platform fee plus recurring, or usage like hosted?
[08:25] Aisha Patel: Private has a platform fee for the private deployment + usage and reserved capacity pricing options. We'll include an indicative pricing sheet with the deck.
[08:35] Samir Rao: For SOC2 and compliance docs, can you email the security pack?
[08:39] Aisha Patel: Yes, we'll send SOC2 summary, penetration test summary, and a compliance pack.
[08:45] Priya Shah: Ok quick run-through of immediate blockers: 1) CIDR overlap with partner X, 2) firewall allowlist for payment rails needs static egress, 3) KMS vendor is AWS KMS, 4) need SSO integration.
[08:57] Connor Lee: For CIDR overlap we'll recommend PrivateLink or NAT/proxy. For egress static IPs use your NAT or Redwood-managed egress add-on. KMS with AWS KMS is supported and SSO is supported.
[09:09] Maria Gomez: Great. Let's recap next steps.
[09:12] Aisha Patel: Recap: we'll send architecture deck + SOC2 excerpt, Connor will schedule networking deep-dive and share VPC peering vs PrivateLink diagram, and Priya will share subnet ranges and KMS details. We'll target getting the items over in the next week.
[09:28] Samir Rao: Sounds good.
[09:30] Aisha Patel: Anything else from Solaris team?
[09:33] Priya Shah: Not from me.
[09:35] Ethan Wu: No.
[09:36] Maria Gomez: No.
[09:37] Aisha Patel: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up by email with docs and booking the deep dive.
[09:42] Call ends.
